Question: What are your thoughts on immigration? Should it be stopped completely or just limited to certain countries?
Answer: Immigration is the process of people moving, on a permanent basis, from one place to another. And our ancestors have been doing it since the dawn of time. Our pre-historic ancestors moved to follow herds of various wild animals or to seek out better pastures etc. Immigration is an essential part of growth of human society. Everywhere you can see the impact of immigration. We use a language from present day England which grew there because of immigration from present-day Germany and France. We use numbers invented in India and then taken by Arabs to Europe. One of my favorite dishes is okra with potatoes which has been perfected in India but potatoes are native to Peru and okra is native to eastern Africa. LA is the birthplace of Korean tacos and San Francisco is the birthplace of “Chinese” fortune cookies. If we stop immigration completely and everyone lives where their ancestors have lived, it would be an ossified place and I am not sure it would be any fun.

Question: If the American healthcare insurance system is so bad, why is it not being reformed and revalidated even after years of seeing the bad side of it?
Answer: Many years ago, I got my first job in Germany. I landed in Frankfurt/Main as a freshly minted engineer and joined a company where everyone else (all 6,000 of them) had some genetic or residential connection to Germany. I had a STEEP learning curve ahead of me. On my second day, my boss told me that my payroll was active, I need to go to Mr X to get a company ID and that I was enrolled in health insurance. So, like any American would, I asked what the deductible was, what was the co-pay and how do I find doctors that are considered in-network. My boss (and later my colleagues) thought that I was making up these words. Some time later, my jaw started hurting and I went to see a dentist and got one wisdom tooth extracted. I paid nothing. The dentist saw my company ID and sent the bill to the appropriate person and that was it. Now, some time later, I was back in the US and was telling people about the health insurance system and they thought I was making it all up. They flat-out refused to believe that I could just go to any dentist and, just on the basis of my company ID, would treat me and I just walk out! I don’t pay a single penny and I don’t give them a credit card. US, unfortunately, is getting ossified. Changes are hard to do and even when a state manages to make some meaningful changes, SCOTUS steps in and invents (they call it “originalism”) philosophies out of thin air and squashes them.
